analysis:
The only change in this PR is a docs-only addition to docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines ~1028-1040). It documents a new `Traffic:` line in `darkbloom status` that reports whether the coordinator can route work to this connection, how long a connection has been down, and the cause when work is not being received (disconnected, no verdict after 90s, expired lease, locked login keychain, stalled Apple call, App Attest unavailable, or no linked account). It references ServingReadiness.swift and StatusCommand+Traffic.swift, neither of which is in the supplied evidence, so the actual implementation is unreviewed.

The prose changes no security control. It describes local status output from the daemon state file and a coordinator-supplied reason string. The related threat entries are T-053, T-057 and T-058 (diagnostics may leak or misstate trust) and A-016 (serving authorization), plus A-018 for the add-on hold interaction. The doc says the line reports App Attest lease or legacy verification eligibility, which could misstate trust if the code overclaims. That is a question for whoever reviews the Swift implementation, not evidence of a regression here.

The other supplied units (base text lines 1728-2005 and head text lines 1-396) are unchanged context describing paths, env passthrough and prefix-cache defaults. They are consistent with the threat-model entry T-041, and I found no change to the SSD cache TTL, key derivation or gating. The doc contains no secrets.

Open question for the next pass: if the Swift implementation surfaces a coordinator-provided reason string verbatim, that string should be sanitized. It is not visible here.
